The human has 6 - level content citizens and one more unhappy per E = (government pair + 2) × (7 - level) cities, staggered by city; the computer players always have 3 and no penalty (v474.05 CityWorker.cs L1433-L1437). Resolves the L33 TODO (civ-clone/web-renderer#173).

Civilization's `cityID` is the city's slot among everyone's cities, not among the player's own, and it decides how many of the human's cities take the extra unhappy citizen, not only which. With another civilization founding between each of theirs, every number is even, and E + 1 cities add nobody. Uses the city's place in the city registry, and keeps the city count per player. Raised by Copilot on #8.

The five levels, `isHuman`, the per-level numbers (content citizens, production ratio; King when no level is set) and the rule that scales the computer players' build costs by ratio/10 (civ-clone/web-renderer#173).

advances × R, R = 6 + 2 × level for the human (at least 11 - advances) and 14 - level for the computer, plus the AD catch-up term, doubled in AD (v474.05 CityWorker.cs L3662-L3690). A turn-start rule works the cost out again, as it changes with the year (civ-clone/web-renderer#173).

`civ1-player:player/turn-start/process-city-yields` adds the cities' research at `High` (1000), and `PlayerResearch.add()` checks completion as it goes, so the recompute at the default `Normal` ran too late: on the first AD turn an advance could complete at its BC price. It now runs at 900. Raised by Copilot on #2.

`BuildItem.cost()` takes the first `BuildCost` result, so a rule that scales every cost for a city (Civ1 difficulty levels: the computer pays ratio/10) can't be another `BuildCost`. Each matching `BuildCostModifier` receives the cost the previous one returned (civ-clone/web-renderer#173).

A ruleset declares its levels as `Difficulty` subclasses in `AvailableDifficultyRegistry`; a game holds its level as one `GameDifficulty` entity in `GameDifficultyRegistry`, so it is saved (civ-clone/web-renderer#173).
`option()` fell back on any falsy value, so a 0-based setting (a difficulty level of 0, Chieftain) read as the default (civ-clone/web-renderer#173).
From the new core-difficulty: the levels a ruleset offers, and the one the game is played at (civ-clone/web-renderer#173).

`difficulty` is runtime state (one GameDifficulty), `availableDifficulties` a class registry, so a save names its level and resolves it on load. A file written before this has no `difficulty` membership and loads with none set (civ-clone/web-renderer#173).
